{"decision":"OPEN, raised by `req:content-store-for-what-the-graph-points-at`. AMENDED 2026-07-31 after Anthony researched the Rust ecosystem and proposed `object_store` (Apache Arrow, originally InfluxData). The original four-way fork is preserved in the snapshot at `snap:epoch:arrival-delta:dec:where-content-lives`.

WHAT THE RESEARCH CHANGES, and it is more than picking a library. The fork assumed the choice was WHERE — repo, beside the repo, or an external service — and that choosing the service re-opened `dec:repo-file-embedded`. `object_store` presents ONE trait over local filesystem, in-memory, S3, GCS, Azure and HTTP/WebDAV, so the backend becomes RUNTIME CONFIGURATION rather than an architectural commitment. Written once against the trait, reflow2 defaults to local and the no-service property is kept intact, while anyone who wants durability configures a cloud backend without reflow2 knowing or caring. That is exactly the resolution option (c) hypothesised — "possibly only for the OPTIONAL half" — arriving as a property of the library rather than as a compromise.

VERIFIED, not taken from the summary: `fs` (LocalFileSystem) is a DEFAULT feature and `InMemory` needs no feature at all; the cloud backends are behind `aws`/`azure`/`gcp` and are NOT default, and with them off the crate avoids pulling `reqwest` and the crypto providers. The in-memory backend also mirrors reflow2's own `open_in_memory` testing idiom, so tests need no filesystem.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and this is the residue that still needs Anthony's word: whether the local blobs are COMMITTED TO THE REPO or GITIGNORED. That is a git question, entirely orthogonal to which crate does the I/O, and it is the one that decides whether a diagram travels with a clone. `object_store` is indifferent to it. Options (a) and (b) from the original fork therefore survive unchanged; (c) and (d) are largely absorbed.

THE REAL COST, which the ecosystem summary does not mention and which bites here specifically: `object_store` IS ASYNC, and `fs` pulls tokio — so even the local-only case requires a runtime. `reflow2-core` is deliberately SYNCHRONOUS: measured 2026-07-31, its entire dependency list is dynograph-{core,storage,graph,resolution,vector}, serde, serde_json and sha2, with no tokio, no async and no futures anywhere. Putting the store in the core would drag a runtime into the one crate that has kept itself deterministic and surface-agnostic.

THE PLACEMENT THAT KEEPS THAT PROPERTY, and it follows the architecture already in place rather than inventing a rule: the CONTENT HASH lives in the core — sync, deterministic, in-memory-testable, exactly what a pointer is — and the STORE lives in `reflow2-mcp`, which already carries tokio through rmcp and hyper. This is the same split as `coverage_report`, where the core computes and the agent supplies what it observed, and the same reason the core is described as neutral to the interaction surface.

STILL TO CHECK BEFORE ADOPTING: `object_store`'s MSRV against the workspace's 1.94, and its transitive tree with cloud features off measured rather than assumed. And per `dec:design-dependencies-declared`, a new dependency is DECLARED with its version and the features taken by name, not just added to a Cargo.toml.

WHAT ANY ANSWER MUST HOLD, unchanged: the pointer is a CONTENT HASH and not a path, because `cap:session-memory` already recorded what a path costs — "a path stored as identity resolves for one person on one machine and silently misses for everyone on a shared graph". And a missing blob must fail LOUD and be nameable (`req:no-silent-fallback`).

THE QUESTION NOW, narrowed from the original: adopt `object_store` with a local default — and do the local blobs get COMMITTED, so a clone carries the diagrams, or GITIGNORED, so the repo stays light?","name":"OPEN — where the bytes behind a pointer live; object_store dissolves most of the fork and leaves one git question","rationale":"Amended rather than answered, and the amendment is worth more than the original because it narrows the question instead of adding to it: a four-way architectural fork became one crate choice plus one git question.

The general shape is worth keeping. The original fork treated "external blob store" and "no service" as opposed, and they are only opposed if the storage backend is baked into the design. A library whose whole purpose is to make the backend a runtime detail removes the opposition rather than resolving it — which is a reminder that some design forks are artifacts of assuming an implementation, and dissolve when the implementation space is actually surveyed.

The async finding runs the other way and is the reason this is still not a trivial adoption: it was found by measuring `reflow2-core`'s dependency list rather than by reading about the crate, and it constrains WHERE the code can go regardless of which backend is chosen. Anthony's research answered the storage question; the constraint it collides with was already in the repo.","status":"proposed"}
